hypothesis: Recognizing provenance-bound Codex CLI 503, internal-server reconnect, and high-demand responses as provider failures will prevent upstream outages from generating local workflow repair tasks while leaving unclassified local failures actionable.

metricsCompared.name: historical progress-reviewer 503 classification
metricsCompared.baseline: The three cited failures had no failureKind and crossed the consecutive local-failure threshold.
metricsCompared.candidate: The exact codex_cli_error response classifies as provider and the detector returns no persistent pattern.

metricsCompared.name: untrusted 503 text classification boundary
metricsCompared.baseline: No provenance-bound parser existed for Codex backend response statuses.
metricsCompared.candidate: Only codex_cli_error subtype or the runtime-owned wrapped prefix plus the exact Codex responses URL enables HTTP status classification.

metricsCompared.name: operator escalation payload contract
metricsCompared.baseline: Future local failure escalations named the repair task id and omitted cost data.
metricsCompared.candidate: The existing workflow fixture continues to assert the generated task id is present and cost and throughput fields are absent.

rationale: Commit 0eb76a9f5 landed after this task was generated and directly addresses its cited evidence. The classification is grounded in the exact status, Codex backend URL, and runtime-owned provenance instead of a broad Service Unavailable text match. Focused tests cover the runtime classifier, aggregate actionable-evidence gate, persistent-pattern detector, and operator attention payload. No threshold was weakened and unrelated 503 text remains unclassified.
